questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) With reference to Algorithm, explain what you understand by the term peudocode. (1 mark)

(b) Describe a source code and an object code (2 marks)

(c) Explain time complexity and space complexity with respect to algorithm design. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Pseudocode (1 mark).** Pseudocode is a way of writing the steps of an algorithm in **structured, English-like statements** (INPUT, IF ... THEN ... ELSE, WHILE, OUTPUT) that is **not tied to any programming language**. It cannot be run by a computer; it is used to plan and explain the logic, and it is easy to convert into a program afterwards.

**(b) Source code and object code (2 marks).**

- **Source code** is the **set of instructions written by the programmer in a high-level language** (for example C, Pascal, Python) or in assembly language. It is readable by humans but cannot be executed directly by the processor.
- **Object code** is the **machine-language (binary) version of the program produced by a compiler or assembler from the source code**. It can be executed by the processor (after linking) but is not readable by humans.

**(c) Time complexity and space complexity (2 marks).**

- **Time complexity** measures **how the running time of an algorithm (the number of basic steps it executes) grows as the size n of the input grows**, written for example O(n) or O(n^2).
- **Space complexity** measures **how much memory (storage for variables, arrays and other data structures) the algorithm needs as the size of the input grows**.

The two are used to **compare algorithms and choose the most efficient one**: a good design uses little time and little memory.

questions.enonce_markdown:
One type of system software is device driver.

(a) Describe device driver and give one example. (2 marks)

(b) State three other types of system software and give examples of each. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Device driver (2 marks).** A device driver is a **small program (system software) that lets the operating system communicate with and control a hardware device**: it translates the general commands of the operating system into the specific instructions that the device understands. Without the correct driver the device does not work properly. *Example:* a printer driver, a graphics (video) card driver, a sound card driver or a network card driver.

**(b) Three other types of system software (3 marks, with examples).**

| Type | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Operating system** | Manages the hardware and software resources and provides the user interface. | Microsoft Windows, Linux, macOS, Android |
| **Utility programs** | Carry out maintenance tasks on the computer. | Antivirus, disk defragmenter, backup software, file compression (WinRAR) |
| **Language translators** | Convert a program written in a programming language into machine code. | Compiler (GCC), interpreter (Python), assembler |

(Firmware such as the BIOS, and linkers and loaders, are also accepted.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is computer ergonomics? (1 mark)

(b) Explain two measures that can be used to prevent RSI. (2 marks)

(c) Apart from RSI explain the cause and effects of two other health problems associated with the use of computers. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Computer ergonomics (1 mark).** Computer ergonomics is the **study and design of computer workstations (desk, chair, monitor, keyboard, mouse, lighting) so that they fit the user**, to give comfort and efficiency and to prevent injury and discomfort.

**(b) Two measures to prevent RSI (repetitive strain injury) (2 marks)** (any two, each explained):

- **Take regular short breaks and do stretching exercises** (for example every 30 to 60 minutes), so that the hands, wrists and arms are not kept doing the same movements for long periods.
- **Use ergonomic equipment and a good posture:** an ergonomic keyboard and mouse, a wrist rest, an adjustable chair, and the keyboard placed at elbow height so that the wrists are kept straight.
- Reduce the amount of continuous typing (for example by using voice recognition software).

**(c) Two other health problems (2 marks, one mark each: cause and effects).**

- **Eye strain (computer vision syndrome).** *Cause:* looking at the screen for a long time without rest, glare and reflections on the screen, poor lighting or a badly adjusted screen. *Effects:* tired, dry and red eyes, headaches and blurred vision.
- **Back and neck pain.** *Cause:* sitting for many hours in a bad posture, on a chair that is not adjustable, or with the screen at the wrong height. *Effects:* pain in the back, neck and shoulders and, in the long term, spine problems.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following terms as use in ICT.

(a) Telemedicine. (1 mark)

(b) Videoconferencing. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Telemedicine (1 mark).** Telemedicine is the **use of ICT (telephone, Internet, video calls, remote monitoring) to provide medical consultation, diagnosis and treatment to patients at a distance**, for example a doctor in Yaounde advising a health worker in a remote village.

**(b) Videoconferencing (1 mark).** Videoconferencing is a **live two-way audio and video communication between people in different places over a network**, using cameras, microphones, screens and software (for example Zoom or Google Meet), so that they can hold meetings or lessons without travelling.
